subject: Runtime guard exception request — toolcall timeouts
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.m@finsecure.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finsecure.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 18:14:02 -0700
Subject: Request: runtime guard exception for toolchain timeouts

Hi Rishi,

During our Canary deployment of the payment-assistant workflow this afternoon we saw repeated tool-call failures originating from Redwood's content-filtering path. The behavior: the request reached Redwood, the filter triggered an async tool invocation path and the toolcall either timed out or returned an error, which cascaded back to the user resulting in 30-40% error rate for affected flows and a 400ms median latency increase overall. We captured logs and a screenshot attached.

We need two things from Redwood immediately:
- A short-term exception (SLA carve-out) to cover the window of 2026-05-20 15:32 - 2026-05-20 17:18 PDT while we investigate. We will need the exception formally documented for our compliance team.
- A plan to avoid the same regression in the next rollout (preferably a routing/fallback that skips the offending filter path).

Attached: traffic-logs-2026-05-20.csv, screenshot-tool-failure.png

Can you confirm receipt and next steps? Amit and I are on standby.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Sr. Product Manager — Payments
FinSecure
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.m@finsecure.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finsecure.com>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 18:32:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: runtime guard exception for toolchain timeouts

Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. I’ve pulled initial traces and see the same pattern you described: when the content guard matches specific patterns it triggers the async toolcall chain and a small subset of requests hit a timeout path under heavier concurrency.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- I’m escalating this to SE + Infra and will propose a temporary routing override to send affected routes to a non-filtered variant while we root-cause.
- Can you confirm whether you want the carve-out to be just for the error window you listed or for the whole Canary (we can do either — the carve-out affects SLA attribution only, not data retention or auditability).
- I’ll follow up with a proposed exception addendum (doc) and suggested mitigations within the hour.

Ben / Karthik — looping you in to propose a 30–60 minute hotfix we can apply to FinSecure’s dedicated pool: short-term routing override + increased toolcall timeout, plus exhaustive log collection. Internal notes/live debugging to follow.

Rishi Malhotra
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Internal-only: FinSecure Canary saw a spike of toolcall timeouts tied to content-filter matches. They want a documented carve-out for 2026-05-20 15:32–17:18 PDT.

Ben — can you draft the routing override and the exact command sequence to toggle for the dedicated pool? We need: 1) temporary rule to bypass content-guard for the payment-assistant route, 2) bump the toolcall timeout from 1.5s to 3s for that route, 3) collection of full KV/caching traces for the problematic prefix.

Karthik — if this looks like kernel-level queuing under concurrency we may need a short autoscale bump and to mark this as a potential runtime optimization (batch shaping). If we grant a carve-out we should also produce a mitigation acceptance checklist for FinSecure.

Subject: Proposed exception addendum & mitigation plan (FinSecure)

Elena — following our investigation and the short-term mitigation we applied (routing override for payment-assistant + timeout bump), please find the formal exception proposal attached: runtime-exception-addendum-v1.docx. Summary below: 

1) Exception window proposed: 2026-05-20T15:32:00Z — 2026-05-20T17:18:00Z (UTC). Please confirm if you prefer PDT timestamps; we will canonicalize in the addendum.
2) Scope: SLA attribution only. Redwood will not count errors attributable to content-filter-induced async toolcall timeouts within the window toward uptime/latency SLA calculations for the payment-assistant route.
3) Mitigations performed: routing override (bypass content guard) applied at 2026-05-20T18:01:12-07:00; toolcall timeout increased to 3s; traffic dump and KV cache traces saved.
4) Follow-up actions (to be completed within 7 business days): a) root-cause postmortem with concrete fix or quantization/profile change; b) one automated fallback route (skip-filter) added to the customer config; c) optional training session for FinSecure engineers on routing policies.
4) Credits: If agreed, Redwood will provide a one-time SLA credit equivalent to 3 days pro-rated for the affected route (applies if formal addendum signed).

Attachments: runtime-exception-addendum-v1.docx (legal-friendly addendum), traffic-logs-2026-05-20.csv (for reference).

If these terms look good I can issue the DocuSign link and route this through our legal for signature today.

Thanks — appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
